title: Live Animal Export Restriction and Prohibition Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would end Australian exports of livestock for slaughter from 1 July 2017 and impose additional animal treatment requirements during the transition period.
Before the ban, exports would generally require the Secretary to be satisfied about holding, transport and slaughter conditions, including stunning immediately before slaughter.
Temporary exemptions could apply to contracts made before commencement, with different requirements for exports within three months and those between three and six months.
changes: Export licence holders would have to take reasonable steps to secure compliance with the specified international animal health guidelines.
Licence holders discovering treatment breaches would need to notify the Secretary within 14 days.
Licences would cease authorising exports for slaughter after the specified end date.
The legislation would begin on Royal Assent.
summary.affected: Livestock export licence holders, exporters with existing contracts, farmers and the Secretary administering export approvals are affected.
